examples.question_text: A car travels $480$ km using $32$ L of fuel. Find its fuel consumption (a) in km/L and (b) in L/100 km. Round non-exact answers to $2$ decimal places.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\frac{480\text{ km}}{32\text{ L}}=\frac{15\text{ km}}{1\text{ L}}$.
The rate is $15$ km/L.
(b) $\frac{32\text{ L}}{480\text{ km}}=\frac{x\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}$.
$x=\frac{32}{480}\times100$.
$x\approx6.67$ L.
The rate is $6.67$ L/100 km, to two decimal places.

examples.question_text:
A car uses $7.2$ L/100 km.
(a) How much fuel does it need for $375$ km?
(b) How far can it travel on $36$ L?
examples.solution_text:
(a) $\frac{7.2\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}=\frac{x\text{ L}}{375\text{ km}}$.
$x=7.2\times\frac{375}{100}=27$ L.
(b) $\frac{7.2\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}=\frac{36\text{ L}}{x\text{ km}}$.
Take reciprocals: $\frac{100\text{ km}}{7.2\text{ L}}=\frac{x\text{ km}}{36\text{ L}}$.
$x=\frac{100}{7.2}\times36=500$ km.

examples.question_text: A car uses $6.4$ L/100 km on a $425$ km trip. Fuel costs $187.5$ cents per litre. Find the fuel cost.
Car A uses $6.3$ L/100 km and Car B uses $7.1$ L/100 km. How much less fuel does Car A use on an $850$ km trip?
examples.solution_text:
Car A: $\frac{6.3\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}=\frac{x\text{ L}}{850\text{ km}}$.
$x=6.3\times\frac{850}{100}$.
$x=53.55$ L.
Car B: $\frac{7.1\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}=\frac{y\text{ L}}{850\text{ km}}$.
$y=7.1\times\frac{850}{100}$.
$y=60.35$ L.
Fuel saving $=60.35-53.55$.
Car A uses $6.8$ L less fuel.

examples.question_text:
A car uses $6.8$ L/100 km on country roads and $9.2$ L/100 km in the city. Its $350$ km journey includes $50$ km of city driving.
(a) Find the total fuel used.
(b) Find the average fuel consumption for the journey in L/100 km, to one decimal place.
examples.solution_text:
Country distance $=350-50=300$ km.
(a) $\frac{6.8\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}=\frac{x\text{ L}}{300\text{ km}}$.
Country fuel $=6.8\times\frac{300}{100}=20.4$ L.
$\frac{9.2\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}=\frac{y\text{ L}}{50\text{ km}}$.
City fuel $=9.2\times\frac{50}{100}=4.6$ L.
Total fuel $=20.4+4.6=25$ L.
(b) $\frac{25\text{ L}}{350\text{ km}}=\frac{z\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}$.
$z=\frac{25}{350}\times100$.
Average rate $\approx7.1$ L/100 km.
Use total fuel divided by total distance, rather than the simple average of the two given rates.

examples.question_text: A workplace is $30$ km from home. A car travels $15$ km/L and fuel costs $\$1.80$ per litre. A bus pass for ten one-way trips costs $\$39$. For ten one-way trips, which option has the lower travel cost, and by how much? Compare fuel cost only for the car.
examples.solution_text:
Total distance $=30\times10=300$ km.
$\frac{15\text{ km}}{1\text{ L}}=\frac{300\text{ km}}{x\text{ L}}$.
Take reciprocals: $\frac{1\text{ L}}{15\text{ km}}=\frac{x\text{ L}}{300\text{ km}}$.
$x=300\div15=20$ L.
Car fuel cost $=20\times1.80=\$36$.
Saving $=39-36=\$3$.
The car has the lower cost for these trips, by $\$3$.

examples.question_text: Amira drives $26$ km to work and $26$ km home on each of $5$ days. Her car uses $7.4$ L/100 km. How much fuel does she use travelling to and from work in a week?
examples.solution_text:
Weekly distance $=26\times2\times5$.
Weekly distance $=260$ km.
$\frac{7.4\text{ L}}{100\text{ km}}=\frac{x\text{ L}}{260\text{ km}}$.
$x=7.4\times\frac{260}{100}$.
$x=19.24$ L.
